text_read: Introduction on the Sadhana (OCR lines 1810-1975) and Appendix A, the Tara sadhana, translation and Sanskrit (OCR lines ~17330-17530 and 17680-17760); grep for pratyaksa/pasyati/clear/visualize.
mode_evidence: Sanskrit colophon: 'yaśca vijanagiriguhāsīnaḥ san bhagavatīṃ bhāvayet, sa khalu pratyakṣata eva tāṃ paśyati' (OCR 'pratyaksatah eva tam _pasyati'), translated by Bhattacharyya 'espies her with his own eyes'. Pratyakṣa means direct perception, so the deity first generated by bhāvanā is claimed to become directly perceived; 'svayam eva bhagavatī tasya śvāsapraśvāsādikaṃ dadāti' adds that she herself gives him breath. It is a promissory claim of result, with no description of how the seeing looks or whether eyes are open.
onset_evidence: The deity is generated from emptiness and the syllable TAM and contemplated 'as long as desired', then meditated on 'repeatedly, until tired'; 'He, who is unable to meditate should mutter the Mantra' (Om Tare Tuttare Ture Svaha). Condition for seeing: practising in a solitary mountain cave. No time scale.

what_to_do_with_light: Keep contemplating; the direct sight of the goddess is presented as a fruit alongside the siddhis and buddhahood.
obstacles_and_fixes: If unable to meditate (visualize), recite the mantra instead
interpretation: The sadhana treats the visualized deity as one with the practitioner yet promises that, in solitude, the goddess becomes directly perceived and acts on him (gives breath).
practice_summary: After refuge and meditation on the purity and voidness of all phenomena, establish voidness with its mantra. In the heart, on a moon within a blue lotus within a moon, see a yellow syllable TAM; from it arises Tara as described in her dhyana. Contemplate her as long as you wish. Rays from TAM invite the eternally accomplished goddess (wisdom being); place her in the sky before you and worship her with water and flowers. Send rays to relieve beings, then meditate on Tara identified with the universe, and return again and again, until tired, to the syllable and the goddess. If you cannot meditate, recite Om Tare Tuttare Ture Svaha. The text promises that one who does this in a solitary mountain cave will see her directly.
